paragraphs.label: Μέρος Αʹ — Ὁ Ἰησοῦς (Part A — Jesus)
paragraphs.translation: After a little time a certain woman comes from the village toward the spring. She has a water jar and comes in order to draw water from the spring.
Jacob rises up and greets her: "Peace to you, O woman. I am very thirsty, I and my donkey. But I have no water jar to draw the water. Are you able to draw water for us from the spring?"
The woman says to him: "Peace to you, O man. I am able to draw water for you."
So then the woman draws water in her jar and provides the water to Jacob so that he may drink.
"I give thanks to you, O woman," says Jacob to her. Then he drinks the water and provides it to the donkey so that he too may drink.
After this, "What is your name?" says the woman.
He answers: "My name is Jacob. And what is your name?"
She says to him: "My name is Salome."

Then again Jacob opens his mouth and says to her: "I give thanks to you, O Salome, because you provide water to me so that I may drink and not be thirsty. Now my body is no longer hungry nor thirsty. For whenever a person is hungry, he eats bread; and whenever he is thirsty, he drinks water. For bread is the food of the body and water is the drink of the body. But I know another food and another drink; this is the food and drink of the spirit. The person has both body and spirit. With the body we eat bread and drink water; but with the spirit we know God and worship him."
Salome marvels and says to him: "What are you saying? I do not know these words."

He says to her: "Yes, I say to you: God is not like the sun or the earth. For he has no body. God is spirit. And we worship him in spirit and in truth. If a person worships God in spirit, God hears him. This is the will of God."
Salome says to him: "I know the God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob."
He says to her: "And I also believe in God, who is the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. But Jesus is the Son of God. For this reason I also believe in Jesus."
Salome says to him: "Now I know that you are a Christian. I know the God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob. And I believe in God, but I do not know Jesus nor do I believe in Jesus."

Jacob says to her: "Yes, I am a Christian; for this reason I believe in Jesus. And I love Jesus; and I follow Jesus; and I hear his voice. For Jesus is the Christ. Not only this, but Jesus is the bread of life, who provides the water of life. Whoever drinks this water will no longer be thirsty, and whoever comes to him will no longer be hungry, because he himself is the bread of life."
Salome marvels and still listens to the words of Jacob.

Jacob says: "And Jesus is the way and the truth and the life; no one comes to God except through him. God is in Jesus and Jesus is in God. Whoever believes in Jesus also believes in God, and whoever follows Jesus also follows God. There are two ways, one of life and one of death. And Jesus is the way of life."
Salome is still silent and says nothing. Jacob sees the fields and trees around the spring, and sees a vine near the spring. The vine has branches, and the branches bear fruit.

He says therefore to Salome: "Do you see that vine, which is near the spring? The vine has branches. If a branch remains in the vine, it bears much fruit. But if it does not remain in the vine, it is not able to bear fruit; for without the vine the branch is nothing."

"In the same way Jesus also is the true vine and his Father is the farmer, and we Christians are like his branches. If we remain in Jesus, we bear much fruit. But if we do not remain in him, we are not able to do anything; for without him we are not able to bear fruit, just as a branch without the vine."

"God, who is the Father of Jesus and ours, loves his Son, and the Son loves us. His love, which is great, remains in us if we believe and follow him. And not only do we love God, but we ought to love one another."

"God is love, and whoever remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him. If we love one another, God remains in us and his love. And there is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear." "If anyone says 'I love God' and hates his brother, he is a liar; we ought to love brothers and sisters."

"And this is the commandment, which is the will of God: that we love one another. Whenever we love one another, we remain in the love of God. And whenever we remain in his love, there is great joy in our hearts."

"If we do this commandment, Jesus says that we are his friends, not servants. Jesus calls us friends. For the servant who works in the field does not know what his master does; but the friend knows. Jesus wants us to know him and his will and his work."
Salome hears all these words. She is silent with her mouth; but the words of Jacob stir up her heart. And she wants to know more.

paragraphs.label: Μέρος Βʹ — Ὁ Ἰησοῦς; (Part B — Jesus?)
paragraphs.translation: After a little while Salome opens her mouth and says to Jacob: "You speak many things about Jesus, O man. But who is this Jesus? I want to know more."

Jacob greatly rejoices in his heart because Salome wants to hear. He says therefore to her: "Yes, O Salome, I say again to you so that you may know. Jesus is the Son of God, who is the Christ. He himself is the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to God the Father except through Jesus. And he himself is the bread of life; whoever believes in him will no longer be hungry nor thirsty forever."

On the road near the spring are the shepherd and the sheep. The shepherd leads the sheep. The sheep follow him. Jacob sees the sheep which eat the grass in the field. He also sees the shepherd who leads and guards them. He says therefore to Salome:

"Do you see these sheep, which eat the grass? And do you see the shepherd who guards them? Jesus is the good shepherd. The good shepherd knows his sheep, and the sheep know the voice of the shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life on behalf of the sheep; he does not flee when the wolf comes, but remains and guards and saves them. In the same way Jesus also lays down his life on behalf of us, because he loves us. We are his sheep, and he himself is our shepherd."

"But the hired worker is not like the good shepherd; the sheep are not his, therefore when the wolf comes, he sees the wolf and abandons the sheep and flees. The wolf therefore seizes them and scatters them. This happens because he is a hireling and does not love the sheep as the good shepherd does."
"Not only is Jesus the good shepherd, but also the door of the sheep. Whoever enters through Jesus — that is, through the door — Jesus saves. And the person has eternal life."
Salome listens and says: "These are good words. But you say that Jesus lays down his life on behalf of us. Why does he do this?"

Jacob says to her: "Because of our sins, O Salome. For all people have sins. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us. But if we confess our sins, God, who is faithful and righteous, forgives us our sins and cleanses us from all unrighteousness. For the blood of Jesus, who is his Son, cleanses us from all sin. We are dead in our sins. Only Jesus is able to save us from our sins."
Salome is silent and still listens. She sees the sheep and the shepherd in the field. Then she sees the light of the sun which comes through the tree.

Jacob speaks again: "And Jesus is the light of the world. For without Jesus, people are in darkness. And Jesus shows us the light. Whoever follows Jesus does not walk in darkness but walks in the light and has the light of life. For Jesus is light, and there is no darkness in him. And the light shines in the darkness and enlightens every person who comes into the world."

"If therefore we say that we have fellowship with God and we walk in darkness, we do not speak the truth. But if we walk in the light, just as God is in the light, we have fellowship with him and with one another, and the blood of Jesus cleanses us. For this is the commandment of God, which we hear always: that we love one another. Whoever loves his brother remains in the light; but whoever hates his brother is in the darkness."
Salome says: "You say these things about Jesus — that he is the bread, the shepherd, the light. But also life? How is he himself the life?"

Jacob answers: "Yes, O Salome. Jesus is the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in him lives, and lives forever. For God, who loves the world, gives his Son to us, so that a person who believes in him may not die but may have eternal life. Jesus therefore is the life and resurrection."
Salome looks at Jacob and says: "You speak many and great words, O Jacob. And your words are good. But I marvel greatly."

Salome is silent again. The sun no longer shines brightly; for evening is coming. Her water jar is still beside the spring, and the water is still in it. But Salome does not worry about the water of the jar; she thinks about the water of life.
